transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in today?

I guess… what finally made me come in is that I just don’t feel like myself anymore. I used to have things that made me feel like me, if that makes sense—painting, hiking when the weather was decent, choir practice, and our Sunday family gatherings. I used to actually look forward to those things and make time for them, even when I was busy.

But now, even if I have a free hour, I don’t do any of it. I’ll just sit there, kind of staring or wasting time, and I can’t seem to make myself care. It’s not that I suddenly hate those things. It’s more like the part of me that wanted them has just… gone quiet. And that’s been really upsetting, because those were the things I always counted on to feel connected and normal.
How long have you been feeling this way, where you don’t take pleasure in the things you used to enjoy?

It’s been… about eight months, I think. Not overnight, exactly. It kind of built up gradually, but if I’m honest, it started around when I took over the STEM-Arts curriculum initiative at school. At first I thought I was just busy or stretched thin because that project was a lot, and I kept telling myself, “Once this settles down, I’ll feel like doing things again.”

But it didn’t really settle, or maybe I didn’t. Since then, month by month, I just noticed I wasn’t reaching for the things I used to enjoy. So… yeah, I’d say about eight months now.
Have you noticed feeling down or sad most of the day, nearly every day, during this time?

Yes… yes, I have. Most days it feels like there’s this heavy gray film over everything. That’s the best way I can describe it. Like I’m going through the motions, but everything is dulled and far away.

And it’s not only when I’m alone, which I think is what scares me. I can be in the classroom, with students talking and needing help, or I can be at home with my husband right there, and I still feel… hollow. Like I’m present physically, but inside I’m just sort of empty and close to tears. Sometimes nothing has even happened, there’s no obvious reason in that exact moment, but I’ll feel this sadness sitting there anyway.
Have you noticed that you feel more fatigued or that you have less energy than usual, even when you haven’t been doing anything physically demanding?

I’m not completely sure how to answer that. I mean, I do feel worn down a lot, but I don’t know if I’d call it fatigue in the way you mean, like physically exhausted from nothing.

Some days I just feel… slowed down, I guess, like it takes more effort to get myself moving or to start the day. But I haven’t really kept track of whether it’s less energy exactly, or just not feeling motivated. Those feel tangled together for me. I’m sorry, I know that’s probably not a very clear answer.
Have you found yourself feeling worthless or guilty, maybe even blaming yourself for things that aren’t your fault, during this time?

Yes… that’s actually been a big part of it, I think. I don’t know if “worthless” is the exact word every time, but I do get this awful feeling that I’m failing people. Especially with the curriculum project.

If anything goes wrong — even something small, like a lesson not landing the way I hoped, or there being some confusion with materials, or a student not engaging — my mind goes straight to, “I’m letting them down.” Not just, “Oh, that didn’t work, adjust it next time,” like I used to be able to think. It becomes this much heavier thing, like I’m somehow wasting their time or failing the students who are depending on me.

And then it spirals into my parents, which probably sounds… I don’t know, dramatic. But my parents sacrificed so much for me to have an education and stable work and opportunities they didn’t really have. So when I’m struggling with this project, I keep thinking, “They worked so hard for me, and this is what I’m doing with it? I’m disappointing everyone.” Even when I can logically see that not everything is my fault, emotionally it still feels like it is.
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite or weight over the past few months—like eating much less or much more than usual, or losing or gaining a significant amount of weight without trying?

I don’t think so… not in any dramatic way, anyway. I haven’t been weighing myself regularly, so I can’t say with certainty that nothing has changed, but I haven’t noticed my clothes fitting very differently or anything like that.

My eating is maybe a little inconsistent just because some days I don’t feel very interested in food, and then other days I’ll eat whatever is easiest because I realize I haven’t really planned anything. But I don’t think I’ve had a clear loss of appetite or a big increase either. It’s more like… I’m not paying as much attention to meals, if that makes sense.

So, no, I wouldn’t say I’ve lost or gained a significant amount of weight without trying. At least not that I’ve noticed.
Have you noticed yourself moving or speaking more slowly than usual, or on the flip side, feeling restless or fidgety without being able to settle down?

I’m not sure I’ve noticed that in a clear way. I don’t think anyone has said to me that I’m speaking slowly, and I haven’t caught myself slurring or anything like that.

I do feel like I take longer to get going sometimes, but I don’t know if that’s the same as actually moving more slowly, if you mean like other people would observe it. It’s more that things feel harder to start. Like I might sit there for a bit before getting up to do something, but once I’m up, I think I move normally? I’m not completely sure.

And the restless side… I wouldn’t say I’m especially fidgety or pacing around unable to settle. I might shift around or get uncomfortable, but not in a way that stands out to me. So I guess my answer is mostly no, or at least not that I’ve really noticed.
Have you ever felt so low or hopeless that you've thought about hurting yourself or that life wasn't worth living?

Yes… I have. I’m kind of scared to say that out loud, but yes.

It’s not that I’ve made a plan or anything like that. I haven’t. But there have been these late nights, especially when I’m alone in the studio and everything is quiet, where my thoughts get really dark. I’ll be sitting there exhausted and overwhelmed, and I’ll catch myself thinking something like, “It would be such a relief if I just didn’t wake up.” Not exactly that I’m trying to do something, but more like… the idea of not having to keep doing all of this feels like relief in that moment.

And then I feel frightened by the fact that I even thought it. Because part of me knows that’s not a normal place for my mind to go, and I don’t want to be alone with it. I actually told my husband because I got scared that I couldn’t keep handling those thoughts by myself. I didn’t tell him every detail at first, because I felt ashamed and I didn’t want to scare him, but I did tell him that I was having thoughts about not wanting to wake up, and that I needed him to know because it was feeling too heavy to carry alone.
Can you describe how your interest in painting, hiking, choir practice, and Sunday family gatherings has changed over the past eight months?

It’s changed a lot. Honestly, that’s probably what finally made me feel like I needed to come in, because I don’t feel like myself anymore.

Painting used to be the thing I would protect time for, even when I was busy. If I had a free hour, I’d think, “Oh good, I can work on something,” or at least sketch or mix colors or even just look through ideas. Now I can have that same free hour and I just… sit there. I’ll look at my supplies and I know, logically, that I used to love it, but I can’t seem to care enough to start. It feels like the part of me that reached for it is just missing.

Hiking is similar. I used to like getting outside, planning little routes, even just being somewhere quiet and green. Now it feels like too much effort, and not in a normal “I’m tired today” way. More like I can’t connect to the reason I used to enjoy it.

Choir practice… I still know it matters, and I know the people there are kind, but I don’t look forward to it the way I did. Singing used to lift me a bit. Now the thought of going feels flat, like another thing I’m supposed to do rather than something I want.

And Sunday family gatherings—those have been hard too. I used to make time for them and feel glad to see everyone, even if it was noisy or a little chaotic. Lately I just don’t have that same pull toward it. I’ll think about going and then feel sort of blank, like I can’t summon the interest or warmth I used to have.

So yes, over the past eight months, those things have really faded for me. It’s not that I suddenly hate them. It’s more unsettling than that—I remember caring about them, but I don’t feel it much anymore.
Have you noticed any significant changes in your sleep lately, like having trouble falling or staying asleep, or sleeping much more than usual?

Yes. My sleep has been really messed up for months now. It’s not just one bad night here and there—it feels like I don’t really know what normal sleep is anymore.

A lot of nights I get into bed and I’m exhausted, but my brain won’t shut off. I’ll lie there going over grant details in my head, like things I need to check, things I might have missed, whether I worded something correctly, whether there’s some deadline or requirement I’m forgetting. It’s ridiculous because I know I’m not actually solving anything at that hour, but I can’t seem to stop replaying it.

And then even if I do fall asleep, I’ll wake up around three or four in the morning. That’s been happening a lot. I’ll wake up with this heavy, alert feeling, like my body thinks there’s some emergency, and then I just lie there watching the time pass. Sometimes I’ll doze a little after that, but it doesn’t feel like real sleep.

There are also times when I sleep longer, or at least I’m in bed longer, but I still wake up feeling like I never actually rested. Like I could have been lying there for eight or nine hours and still feel worn out when I get up. So yes, it’s been pretty significant. It’s one of those things that’s made everything else feel harder, because I start the day already feeling behind.
